title: Payments docs
intro: Payments takes online payments for your customers with your own gateway keys: Stripe, PayPal, PayFast, JazzCash, Easypaisa, manual bank transfer and a generic adapter for any other gateway. Payers always pay on the gateway's own page or form, so card details never touch our servers. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server (or is pasted into Ecommerce).
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https, and return addresses may point there. These pages use your website's real database and gateway keys, so payments made there are real. There is no test mode: use your gateway's own test keys or sandbox if it has one.
payments: Create a payment with the server token: POST /v1/payments with the amount in minor units (cents, paisa …), the currency (ISO 4217), what the payer sees (description), your reference (for example the order id), the payer and where they return (returnUrl and cancelUrl on your website). Name a gateway, or leave it out and the payer picks one of the ready gateways that take the currency. Send the payer to checkoutUrl. Send an Idempotency-Key header so a repeated request is refused instead of making a second payment.
confirm: Never mark an order paid because of what the browser brings back. Payments marks a payment paid only after the gateway confirmed it (a signed notice, or Payments asking the gateway server to server) for the payment's exact amount and currency. Your server then checks with POST /v1/payments/<id>/verify and the amount and currency it expects: verified is true only for a payment of this website paid for exactly that amount. A pending payment is asked of its gateway again when you read it (at most every 30 seconds), so an unconfirmed payment is rechecked without timers.
events: Payment events (payments.payment.paid, payments.payment.failed, payments.payment.refunded, payments.subscription.updated) are listed by GET /v1/events and, with the Notifications token pasted into Connections, sent to your webhook URLs by Notifications (turn on its Outgoing webhooks feature, set the URLs and the signing secret there). Each is a POST of JSON { id, type, createdAt, websiteId, data } with the header SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Check it before trusting the body, then still verify the payment with the API.
gateways: Connect each gateway in the product dashboard (Connections); its keys are encrypted and never shown again. Register the addresses below with the gateway where it asks for them (replace <websiteId> with your website's id, shown in the dashboard's Developers tab).
stripe: Stripe: the secret key (sk_live_…, sk_test_… or a restricted key with Checkout Sessions, Refunds and Subscriptions) and the signing secret of a webhook endpoint at the Stripe address below, with the events checkout.session.completed, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded, checkout.session.async_payment_failed, customer.subscription.created, customer.subscription.updated and customer.subscription.deleted. Payers pay on Stripe Checkout.
paypal: PayPal: the client id and secret of your REST app and the id of a webhook at the PayPal address below, with the events PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED, PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED and BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.*; tick Sandbox for a sandbox app. Payers approve on PayPal's page and Payments captures the order.
payfast: PayFast: your merchant id, merchant key and the passphrase set in your PayFast account (the API needs it); tick Sandbox for a sandbox account. Payments sends PayFast the notice address below with every payment, so there is nothing to register. Takes ZAR.
jazzcash: JazzCash: your merchant id, password and integrity salt; tick Sandbox for the sandbox. JazzCash posts its signed answer back to the return address below (one per payment); if JazzCash asks for your return URL, give it this address. Takes PKR. Refunds are recorded in Payments; return the money in the JazzCash portal.
easypaisa: Easypaisa (Easypay): your store id, hash key, API user name and password and account number; tick Sandbox for the staging site. Easypay sends the payer back to the return address below (one per payment); Payments then asks Easypay's inquire-transaction API whether it was paid. Takes PKR. Refunds are recorded in Payments; return the money in the Easypay portal.
generic: Generic adapter (any other gateway, or your own bridge to one): a name payers see, the https checkout address, a secret of at least 24 characters and, if the gateway can refund, a refund address. The payer's browser posts payment_id, website_id, amount (minor units), currency, description, return_url, cancel_url, notify_url, timestamp and signature (hex HMAC-SHA256 with the secret over the other fields sorted by name as name=value joined by &). Confirm by posting JSON { paymentId, status: paid | failed | cancelled, amount, currency, reference } to notify_url with SS-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<body>">. Refunds are posted to the refund address as signed JSON { refundId, paymentId, reference, amount, currency, reason }; without one they are recorded only.
bank: Bank transfer: the payer sees your bank details (Settings) and the payment's reference; with Proof upload on and Storage connected, they can upload a photo or PDF of the transfer straight to your storage (allow your Payments address in the bucket's CORS for PUT). You confirm receipt with the Payments admin widget or POST /v1/payments/<id>/confirm; GET /v1/payments/<id>/proof gives a 5-minute link to the proof.
currencies: Each payment has its own currency. Stripe and bank transfer take any ISO 4217 code (Stripe refuses the few it does not support); PayPal takes its listed currencies; PayFast ZAR; JazzCash and Easypaisa PKR; the generic adapter what its connection lists (else any). The pay page offers only gateways that take the payment's currency.
links: Payment links are for any amount: invoices, bookings, donations. POST /v1/links with a title, the currency and an amount (or null to let the payer enter it, at least minAmount). Share its url (a page Payments hosts, with every word editable in Settings → Texts) or place the pay button with data-link on your own page. PATCH /v1/links/<id> with { active: false } stops it.
refunds: Refund all or part of a paid payment with POST /v1/payments/<id>/refunds { amount?, reason? } (no amount: everything left) or the Payments admin widget. Stripe, PayPal, PayFast and a generic gateway with a refund address refund through the gateway; the others are recorded in the payment's history and you return the money yourself.
subscriptions: Subscriptions are managed by the gateway: create the plan in Stripe (a recurring price) or PayPal (a billing plan), then POST /v1/subscriptions { gateway, plan, customer, returnUrl } and send the payer to checkoutUrl. Payments mirrors the status from the gateway's notices; the Subscriptions admin widget and POST /v1/subscriptions/<id>/cancel cancel at the gateway.
install: Add the script to your pages and place the pay button: with data-link for a payment link, or with data-payment for a payment your server created. The button renders nothing while its feature is off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: the Payments admin (payments.read; refund with payments.refund; confirm transfers with payments.confirm) and the Subscriptions admin (subscriptions.read, subscriptions.cancel). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Amounts are integer minor units with a currency. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
